key_insight: MoE expert outputs exhibit structured redundancy, enabling pruning that preserves shared functional and distributional structure rather than ranking experts independently.
engineering_relevance: Structure-preserving expert pruning targets the storage overhead of MoE deployment while retaining performance on general and mathematical reasoning tasks.
method: Use greedy expert subset selection with router-derived importance weights.
PEEP maximizes weighted projection energy to preserve the functional subspace.
DCEP minimizes weighted coverage error to preserve distributional geometry.
evidence_signal: On DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Qwen3-30B-A3B at 75% and 50% expert retention, the methods outperform baselines on most benchmarks and achieve the best average performance across general and mathematical reasoning tasks.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify pruning overhead, deployment memory savings, or inference speedups.
paper_title: Experts Exhibit Structured Redundancy: Structure-Preserving Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models
